title: Article 140 — Ancillary powers of Supreme Court

content.overview: Article 140 provides that Parliament may by law make provision for conferring upon the Supreme Court such supplemental powers not inconsistent with any of the provisions of the Constitution as may appear to be necessary or desirable for the purpose of enabling the Court more effectively to exercise the jurisdiction conferred upon it by or under the Constitution.
content.glance: Parliament may by law confer supplemental powers on SC (not inconsistent with the Constitution) to enable more effective exercise of its jurisdiction.
content.study:
Article 140 is an enabling provision for ancillary/supplemental powers. Any such powers must not be inconsistent with the Constitution and must be for enabling more effective exercise of jurisdiction already conferred by or under the Constitution.

Examination: parliamentary law; supplemental; consistency with Constitution; purpose = effective exercise of existing jurisdiction.

sections.heading: Key rule
sections.body: Parliament may by law confer on the SC supplemental powers not inconsistent with the Constitution, necessary or desirable for more effective exercise of jurisdiction conferred by or under the Constitution.

questionsAndAnswers.question: What does Article 140 provide?
questionsAndAnswers.answer: Article 140 provides that Parliament may by law make provision for conferring upon the Supreme Court such supplemental powers not inconsistent with any of the provisions of the Constitution as may appear necessary or desirable for enabling the Court more effectively to exercise the jurisdiction conferred upon it by or under the Constitution.

examTips: Supplemental powers by parliamentary law; must fit existing jurisdiction.

keyTakeaways: Art 140: parliamentary power to confer ancillary SC powers.
